chapters.title: A production schedule is a decision about the future
What ERP knows and where execution takes over
Measuring, context and learning from plan versus actual
Replanning, the closed loop and why Excel survives
Production context: machine stops, material, quality and finite capacity
Dashboards, Microsoft Fabric, OT data, digital twins and knowledge graphs
Industrial AI, the planner's role and event-driven replanning

takeaways: A released ERP schedule is a decision based on yesterday's facts, so it needs a closed feedback loop of execution, measurement, learning and replanning to stay feasible.

Production events only become useful when they connect to order, operation, resource and time through explicit product, process and resource relationships, with shared definitions for words like complete and available.

Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, digital twins, knowledge graphs and industrial AI can support the loop, but feasible replans still need explicit constraints, trigger rules, freeze windows and named human decision rights.
hook: Production schedules look solid when they leave ERP, yet material delays, tool issues, missing skills and short machine stops make them outdated before the first order starts. This episode is for manufacturing planners, operations leaders and data architects who keep seeing Excel become the real control system. You will learn how a closed loop of execution data, production context, learning and controlled replanning keeps dispatch decisions feasible.
